newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEFS SIGN FREE AGENT QB ELVIS GRBAC TO FIVE-YEAR DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-CHIEFS SIGN FREE AGENT QB ELVIS GRBAC TO FIVE-YEAR DEAL.

text.p: The Kansas City Chiefs signed unrestricted free agent quarterback Elvis Grbac to a five-year contract, the team announced Monday.
The 26-year-old Grbac had been a backup to Steve Young with the San Francisco 49ers for the last four years, but will move in as the Chiefs starting quarterback.
Grbac posted a 6-3 record with the 49ers in his nine starts in place the injured Young over the last two years.
"What ultimately made my decision was the opportunity to start immediately with the Chiefs," said Grbac.
Grbac's signing continues the trend of 49ers' quarterbacks moving to Kansas City.

Joe Montana played the last two years of his Hall of Fame career with the Chiefs after winning four Super Bowls with San Francisco. Steve Bono followed Montana to Kansas City in a May 1994 trade, resuming his role as Montana's backup before becoming the Chiefs starter in 1995 after Montana retired.
Bono, however, was benched late last season by coach Marty Schottenheimer and the team had been in the market for a new starting quarterback.
Grbac established himself as one of the league's top backup quarterbacks when he posted three consecutive 300-yard games during a string of five successive starts in 1995.
In the 14 games in which Grbac replaced an injured Young, or started for Young, the 49ers went 10-4.
Grbac completed 62.2 percent of his passes last season for 1,236 yards with eight touchdowns and 10 interceptions.
In 43 games with the Niners, Grbac completed 284-of-430 passes, a 66 percent rate, for 3,098 yards and 18 touchdowns with 16 interceptions.
